points.description: States that pandas and koalas are similar because both are specialists with a very narrow diet—pandas eat almost only bamboo and koalas eat almost only eucalyptus.
States that pandas and koalas differ from pythons because pythons are generalists, able to live in many environments, unlike the two specialists.

Explains that “invasive” is significant because it carries a negative judgment or frames nonnative species as harmful spreaders, and this framing is central to the article’s debate—e.g., MacInnes prefers “introduced,” while biologists treat invasive species as threats to biodiversity.

rubric.notes: Full marks require both prompts to be addressed: the Koala/Panda response must give both the similarity and the difference from pythons, and the Invasive Species response must explain the term’s judgment-laden significance in the article’s debate. Part marks are available for only one half of the Koala/Panda comparison. No marks for unsupported or irrelevant answers.
